meta.name: providers
meta.description: Every paid service the system calls, one description each (jav/core/providers.py). `key`: the key it needs, read from the environment (`typesafe`: TypeSafeJAV_API_KEY or TYPESAFE_API_KEY; `openai`: OPENAI_API_KEY; `azure_di`: AZURE_DI_ENDPOINT and AZURE_DI_KEY). `budget`: the provider whose budget its calls reserve from; the call log keeps the provider's own name. `enabled`: whether an installation may call it at all; an installation overrides it with JAV_PROVIDERS_ON / JAV_PROVIDERS_OFF (comma-separated provider names), and `off_note` says why it is off by default. `key_fallback`: how it is still reached without its own key, so a missing key is not reported as a refusal (Azure DI through the legacy sidecar). `label`: its name on screen and in reports. (Glossary: Provider registry.)

changelog.note: Azure DI's `key_fallback`: without its own key it is reached through the legacy sidecar (for the PDFs under the legacy data folder), so a measurement does not say that every Azure call would be refused; no other value changes.

First version: JEV, OpenAI, OpenAI Decisions (OpenAI's judgement service; it spends from the OpenAI budget, the owner's decision of 2026-11-01, and is off until its measurement and the owner's decision) and Azure DI.
